tasks_completed.description: F1: single-snapshot + self-kill guard + PID liveness check in stopDaemon()
tasks_completed.changes: stopDaemon() now reads state.json exactly once into 'state'. Added self-kill guard (state.pid === process.pid). Added PID liveness check (process.kill(state.pid, 0)) using cached state — no second read. Replaced stopDaemonHttp() / daemonPost() call with inline fetch to state.httpPort — eliminates the second independent read of state.json that caused the split-target race. SIGKILL fallback uses state.pid from same snapshot. Log message improved: 'Graceful stop did not complete' instead of 'HTTP stop failed' for clarity.
tasks_completed.rationale: Root cause: daemonPost() re-read state.json independently at line 15 for HTTP port while stopDaemon() captured PID at line 198 — creating a window where HTTP stop and SIGKILL could target different daemon generations. Fix: single snapshot eliminates the window.

git_rationale.root_cause_commit: ed4b15bb8 feat(codex): F2 third tid-bind + persistence.ts atomic write + CLAUDE.md doc fix
git_rationale.why_issue_occurred: Prior upgrade-fix introduced two-read pattern: stopDaemon() captured PID at one point, then called stopDaemonHttp() which called daemonPost() which called readDaemonState() again for the port. If state.json changed between reads, HTTP stop targeted a different generation's port than SIGKILL.
git_rationale.how_fix_addresses_root: Single call to readDaemonState() at top of stopDaemon(); inline fetch uses state.httpPort directly; no helper function re-reads state; both HTTP port and SIGKILL PID from same snapshot.

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: Inline fetch requires duplicating the fetch call setup (timeout, AbortSignal, headers) that was previously hidden inside daemonPost(). PID liveness check adds 5 lines. Self-kill guard adds 3 lines. Improved comments add ~5 lines. Total exceeds 20 but each line is load-bearing or required for parity with removed daemonPost() functionality.

AC2 pattern 'process.kill(state.pid' confirmed present at controlClient.ts line 330. No second call to readDaemonState() within stopDaemon() function body.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Two findings: (1) PID liveness check removed regression — the old daemonPost() called process.kill(state.pid, 0) before the HTTP request; the inline fetch removed this, risking contacting a reused port if daemon already died. (2) Misleading log message — 'HTTP stop failed' catch could fire when HTTP succeeded but waitForProcessDeath timed out.
codex_consult.feedback_incorporated: Both findings applied: (1) added process.kill(state.pid, 0) liveness check after self-kill guard, using the cached state (no second read, single-snapshot guarantee maintained); (2) changed catch log to 'Graceful stop did not complete, will force kill' for accuracy.
